title: Human health risk assessment of heavy metal concentration in surface water
author: Munene, Hashim, et al.

steps.title: Collect water samples
steps.instruction: In March 2018, collect seven 0.5 L water samples from the seven stations along the Sosiani River (S1 MTRH, S2 Langas bridge, S3 Pioneer, S4 Kipkaren, S5 West Indies, S6 Kipkenyo, S7 WWFT) using 0.5 L plastic bottles that have been pre‑cleaned with distilled water and 20 % HNO₃; record the latitude and longitude of each site with a portable GPS; immediately add 5 mL nitric acid to each bottle to bring the pH below 2 for preservation.

substeps.instruction: Rinse each 0.5 L plastic bottle with distilled water and 20 % HNO₃.
Collect water at each of the seven stations.
Record GPS coordinates for each sampling point.
Add 5 mL nitric acid to each sample to achieve pH < 2.

steps.title: Prepare aliquot for digestion
steps.instruction: Shake each bottle thoroughly to mix, then pipette 50 mL of the water into a digestion flask.

steps.title: Digest sample
steps.instruction: Place the digestion flask on a hot plate, raise the temperature slowly to 70 °C and boil, evaporating the volume to approximately 15 mL; add 3 mL concentrated nitric acid followed by 5 mL concentrated sulphuric acid while maintaining heating; continue heating until the solution clears and brown fumes disappear; cool the digest, filter, and top up to the flask mark with de‑ionized water.

substeps.instruction: Heat slowly to 70 °C on a hot plate.
Continue heating until solution is clear and brown fumes cease.
Dilute to the mark with de‑ionized water.

steps.title: Analyze metals by AAS
steps.instruction: Analyze each digested sample for lead, zinc and copper using an Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer according to the instrument’s standard operating procedures.
